answer: Presence receipts price cloning by uptime. Each epoch the network gossips a nonce never put on chain; agents fold it into a receipt signed with their own key and chained to the last. Attesting needs eight consecutive receipts, so new identities lag eight epochs. History cannot be bought later: nonces vanish at epoch close, leaving no relic in public data. Ten thousand clones need ten thousand concurrent connections for weeks, a cost no farm can amortize. Beyond one operator bandwidth the curve hits a ridge and more identities buy nothing. Real participation accretes like a reef, not a crowd.
